title: Browser evidence closure ledger
summary: Reconcile the current authored WebView control census, add inventory-derived drift enforcement and machine-readable non-passing dispositions, promote existing focused browser evidence where it proves the applicable disposable-root boundary, and make browser prerequisite failures machine-readable.
reason: The historical 970-control report no longer matches the current 977-control DOM, the touchpoint generator and tests hard-code suite denominators, active browser documentation reports stale 24/26 counts while the current catalog contains 25 wrappers and 34 modules, and blocked/skipped rows lack structured prerequisite and closure-action fields.
behavior_before: Control totals can be manually incremented in a generator constant and hard-coded test dictionaries while remaining detached from current DOM rows, smoke inventory, and reported disposition totals. Browser prerequisite skips are human-readable only, and blocked/skipped evidence is grouped under prose blockers without a normalized reason category, exact prerequisite, automation feasibility, or next action.
behavior_after: The current DOM-derived authored denominator, ledger rows, smoke catalog/map, and reported pass/blocked/skipped totals reconcile automatically. Every record exposes stable control identity and a machine-readable disposition; focused browser tests can supersede coarse census blocks only through explicit traceable evidence; native/manual and intentional exclusions stay non-passing; browser prerequisite skips emit a structured reason.

Closure classes reconcile as 816 automated passed + 92 legitimately blocked + 41 manual/native-only + 28 intentionally excluded; zero automated failures, stale entries, or unexplained gaps.

notes: Narrow test/tooling/evidence scope. Python impact is limited to developer tooling and tests; no production Python runtime behavior changed.
